topic: How does orbital configuration impact frequency planning trade-offs for RLNC schemes requiring continuous coverage and low latency in multi-user broadcasts?
consensus_response: The orbital configuration significantly impacts frequency planning trade-offs for RLNC schemes. Lower altitudes increase Doppler shift, leading to higher interference and reduced system capacity. The array factor is modulated by the Doppler shift, introducing additional complexity in the design. Hybrid TDMA/CDMA protocols can mitigate inter-satellite interference while minimizing Doppler shift effects on signal processing complexity. Efficient frequency reuse is crucial to minimize interference and maximize system capacity.
